title: Cohomological transfer and equivariant anticanonical sections
main_claim: Theorem 1.1 (Invariant transfer): X is smooth projective with smoothly semipositive -K_X, and a torus T acts on X. Suppose P is -K_X with any linearization, -M is pseudoeffective, and there are nonzero invariant sections of M+iP for unboundedly many i. Then H^0(X,mP)^T is nonzero for some m>0. Corollary 1.2: every such X has a nonzero section of some -mK_X. The proof combines natural invariant nonvanishing (when chi(O) is nonzero) with descent along compact-torus monodromy.

issues.location: sections/descent.tex, proof of Corollary 1.2; sections/cohomological-input.tex, Prop. har:prop:index
issues.description: The headline corollary is only as strong as two companion results, which this paper uses as black boxes. The first is CompanionH: the universal-cover splitting C^c x V x F, with a finite-index deck subgroup acting by translations on C^c, trivially on V and through a compact torus on F, plus the finite etale norm. The second is CompanionI: an invariant anticanonical index that is a polynomial P(m) on multiples of a, with P(0) exactly equal to the invariant chi(O). The paper says it uses only CompanionH's structure statement and not its nonvanishing conclusion, so the argument is not circular. I did not verify either companion here.
issues.evidence: "We use the structure statement of [CompanionH, Theorem (Finite cover with compact torus monodromy)], not that companion's nonvanishing conclusion"; "The following result is the exact input from the index companion [CompanionI]"

issues.description: The proof needs -M to be pseudoeffective, where M is a saturated line subsheaf of wedge^e Omega^{n-q}, and it gets this entirely from LMPTX Theorem 4.1 (a line subsheaf of a tensor power of Omega^1 on a pair with nef -K). The paper's own degree lemma (har:lem:null-divisors) proves only c1(M).G^{n-1} <= 0 for Kahler classes G. That is weaker than pseudoeffectivity, which needs the inequality against movable classes. So this step depends on the cited theorem holding with exactly these hypotheses. I believe it does, but did not check against LMPTX.
issues.evidence: "The cotangent-tensor theorem [LMPTX2023, Theorem 4.1], applied to the smooth zero-boundary pair with nef -K_X, says that -M is pseudoeffective."

coverage:
I read the introduction, models.tex (Lemma val:flat-model and Prop. har:prop:maximum), the whole proof of Theorem 1.1 in transfer.tex, cohomological-input.tex (Prop. har:prop:index, Lemma har:lem:forms, Cor. thm:main, Lemma har:lem:null-divisors) and descent.tex (proof of Cor. 1.2, cohomology and form descent, the tensor-holonomy proposition). I checked these steps in detail:
- The trdeg-0 case, via the affine slope of the section divisors.
- The common ratio field identity, including the degree bookkeeping for the multipliers s_p^{a(b-q-1)}s_b^{a(q-p)}.
- The horizontal-slope effectivity and the vertical normalization that makes gamma regular.
- The proof that the invariant adjoint rank is 1 for all j >= 0. I verified the degree identity kE+k pi^*N_b+f^*(kaH-(b-i-jk)kB), and the base twist is cancelled through ratio-domination.
- That L'-eta f^*H is pseudoeffective, and the Skoda-trivial strict metric h >= c h_0.
- The pushforward density exponent (a+1)/l-1, worked out from y1=z1^l with the Jacobian factor.
- The choice of D_* and the requirement that f^*D_* be exceptional, including primes over codimension >= 2.
- That the weight is bounded above, so it extends as a psh function, and the inclusion O(-D_*) in J.
- Nadel vanishing with a bounded twist, which leaves J unchanged, and the Snapper polynomial being nonzero at 0.
- The continuous maximum metric: L^k moments converging to the maximum, Z_0 of codimension >= 2, and M_e > 0 by Hartogs.
- In descent: the deck-invariant product section and the Galois norm.
I skimmed the Lemma forms argument (hard Lefschetz, determinant saturation). I did not audit the alternative routes in ordinary, harmonic-*, alteration, local-ideal and stabilized; they are not on the shortest path to the main results.
sibling_notes: The board for family 068 had two sibling papers: rank 22 (Metric descent / rank-preserving contractions) and rank 6 (Bounded anticanonical metrics on klt pairs). Both were no_gap_found with only minor cited-hypothesis notes. Rank 6 also relies on LMPTX Thm 4.1 as cited and on a companion finite-cover theorem, which matches this paper's use of LMPTX 4.1 and CompanionH. Nothing on the board changed my assessment.
